title: Top 10 NRS E-Invoicing Platforms in Nigeria in 2027
summary: Compare 10 NRS-accredited e-invoicing platforms in Nigeria for 2027, what SIs and APPs do, and how to choose one that fits your business.
body_markdown:
Since the NRS made e-invoicing mandatory, the question for Nigerian finance teams has changed from “do we have to comply?” to “which platform should we use?” More than 1,000 large taxpayers had onboarded by the first quarter of 2026; the 31 July 2026 deadline for large taxpayers has passed, and the NRS has begun enforcement. Medium taxpayers are next. Every business must connect to the NRS Merchant Buyer Solution (MBS) through an NRS-accredited Systems Integrator (SI) or Access Point Provider (APP), and the wrong choice can delay your go-live and leave your team matching payments to invoices by hand.


This guide covers ten accredited platforms, starting with Duplo, which builds NRS e-invoicing directly into the same platform finance teams use for payments, collections, and reconciliation.


[Get NRS-Compliant With Duplo 🢅](https://app.tryduplo.com/onboarding/?formGuid=a07eca94-c950-4c65-abed-e775940237fesource=blog&medium=content&campaign=nrs_einvoicing11)


### SI vs APP: What Is the Difference?


A Systems Integrator connects your ERP, accounting, or invoicing system to the NRS platform and converts your invoices into the required format. An Access Point Provider handles the secure transmission of invoice data between your business and the NRS. Some providers hold both accreditations, so one provider can handle the full chain.


### Where the NRS E-Invoicing Rollout Stands


**Taxpayer category** **Annual turnover** **Go-live** **Enforcement**


Large ₦5 billion and above November 2025 Deadline 31 July 2026 (passed)


Medium ₦1 billion to ₦5 billion 1 July 2026 Expected January to March 2027


Emerging Below ₦1 billion 1 July 2027 From 2028


*Timeline as set out in the NRS public notice of 17 February 2026. Confirm current dates with the[NRS](https://nrs.gov.ng/) before you plan.*

### Why the Platform You Choose Matters Now


Non-compliance has a direct cost. Under Section 104 of Nigeria’s tax laws, failing to process a taxable supply through the fiscalisation system carries a penalty of ₦200,000, plus 100% of the tax due and interest at the CBN Monetary Policy Rate. Separately, Section 103 sets a penalty of ₦1 million for the first day, and ₦10,000 for each day after, when a business fails to allow the NRS to deploy its technology within 30 days of notice.


There is also a commercial risk. Buyers can only reclaim input VAT on invoices cleared through the MBS, so customers have a reason to move to suppliers that are compliant. A slow or fragile integration delays your go-live, and every week of delay is a week of exposure.


### What a Good NRS E-Invoicing Platform Should Do


- Generate invoices in the prescribed structured format with all mandatory data fields.
- Validate and digitally sign each invoice before it is sent.
- Transmit to the MBS and return a valid IRN for every invoice.
- Check supplier invoices for a valid IRN, since you should only accept compliant invoices.
- Keep a complete audit trail of every transmission.


### How to Choose the Right NRS E-Invoicing Platform


Four questions will narrow the list quickly.


**Does the provider hold the accreditation you need?** A provider with both SI and APP accreditation means one contract and one point of accountability.


**Does it work with your current systems?** Check support for your ERP or accounting software before you commit.


**Does it connect to the rest of your finance workflow?** An invoice that is compliant but disconnected from collections and reconciliation still leaves your team matching payments by hand.


**Is it secure and well supported?** Look for security certifications, data protection compliance, and local support.


Accreditation status changes, so confirm any provider on the NRS approved service providers directory before you sign.

### Frequently Asked Questions


**What is an NRS e-invoicing platform?** It is software from an NRS-accredited Systems Integrator or Access Point Provider that generates, validates, and transmits your invoices to the NRS Merchant Buyer Solution.


**Do I need both an SI and an APP?** You need both functions covered. Some providers, including Duplo, hold both accreditations, so one provider can handle the full chain.


**Who must comply with NRS e-invoicing?** Compliance is phased by turnover. Large taxpayers with ₦5 billion and above have passed their 31 July 2026 deadline. Medium taxpayers went live on 1 July 2026, and emerging taxpayers follow in 2027.


**Are PDF invoices compliant?** No. Invoices must be structured files validated through the MBS and carry a valid IRN.
